sanskrit.deva:
ऋतं पिबन्तौ सुकृतस्य लोके गुहां प्रविष्टौ परमे परार्धे ।
छायातपौ ब्रह्मविदो वदन्ति पञ्चाग्नयो ये च त्रिणाचिकेताः ॥ १ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
ṛtaṃ pibantau sukṛtasya loke guhāṃ praviṣṭau parame parārdhe |
chāyātapau brahmavido vadanti pañcāgnayo ye ca triṇāciketāḥ || 1 ||

lines.iast: ṛtaṃ pibantau sukṛtasya loke guhāṃ praviṣṭau parame parārdhe
lines.deva: ऋतं पिबन्तौ सुकृतस्य लोके गुहां प्रविष्टौ परमे परार्धे

lines.iast: chāyātapau brahmavido vadanti pañcāgnayo ye ca triṇāciketāḥ
lines.deva: छायातपौ ब्रह्मविदो वदन्ति पञ्चाग्नयो ये च त्रिणाचिकेताः

padaccheda.iast: ṛtam pibantau sukṛtasya loke guhām praviṣṭau parame parārdhe chāyā-ātapau brahma-vidaḥ vadanti pañca-agnayaḥ ye ca triṇāciketāḥ
padaccheda.deva: ऋतम् पिबन्तौ सुकृतस्य लोके गुहाम् प्रविष्टौ परमे परार्धे छाया-आतपौ ब्रह्म-विदः वदन्ति पञ्च-अग्नयः ये च त्रिणाचिकेताः

words.meaning: of what one has oneself done

grammar.en: past passive participle m. acc. du.

words.meaning: those who keep the five fires
those who have thrice built the Nāciketa fire

translations.text: “There are two who drink the sure fruit of their own deeds in this world, who have entered the cave, in the supreme abode of the highest. The knowers of Brahman call them shade and light; so do those who keep the five fires and those who have thrice built the Nāciketa fire.”

notes: Śaṅkara: the two are the individual self and the supreme Self. Only one of them tastes the fruit of action, but both are said to ‘drink’, as a whole company is called ‘the people with umbrellas’ when only some carry them. ṛta is ‘truth’, the fruit of action, because it is certain to come. loke: in this body. The cave is the intellect; parārdha, ‘the place of the highest Brahman’, is the space within the heart, where Brahman is perceived. Shade and light: unlike each other, as one is bound to the cycle of birth and death and the other is not. Those of the five fires are householders.

sanskrit.deva:
यः सेतुरीजानानामक्षरं ब्रह्म यत्परम् ।
अभयं तितीर्षतां पारं नाचिकेतं शकेमहि ॥ २ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yaḥ setur ījānānām akṣaraṃ brahma yat param |
abhayaṃ titīrṣatāṃ pāraṃ nāciketaṃ śakemahi || 2 ||

lines.iast: yaḥ setur ījānānām akṣaraṃ brahma yat param
abhayaṃ titīrṣatāṃ pāraṃ nāciketaṃ śakemahi

padaccheda.iast: yaḥ setuḥ ījānānām akṣaram brahma yat param abhayam titīrṣatām pāram nāciketam śakemahi
padaccheda.deva: यः सेतुः ईजानानाम् अक्षरम् ब्रह्म यत् परम् अभयम् तितीर्षताम् पारम् नाचिकेतम् शकेमहि

words.meaning: of those who wish to cross

translations.text: “May we be able to know the Nāciketa fire, which is the bridge for those who sacrifice; and also the imperishable, supreme Brahman, fearless, the farther shore for those who wish to cross.”

notes: Śaṅkara: the fire is a bridge because it carries those devoted to rites across sorrow; ‘may we be able’ to know it and to build it. The supreme Brahman, called the Self, is the refuge of the knowers of Brahman who wish to cross the cycle of birth and death. Both the lower and the higher Brahman are to be known: these are the two spoken of in the first verse.
titīrṣatām is a desiderative participle; it is labelled here as a present participle.

sanskrit.deva:
आत्मानं रथिनं विद्धि शरीरं रथमेव तु ।
बुद्धिं तु सारथिं विद्धि मनः प्रग्रहमेव च ॥ ३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
ātmānaṃ rathinaṃ viddhi śarīraṃ ratham eva tu |
buddhiṃ tu sārathiṃ viddhi manaḥ pragraham eva ca || 3 ||

lines.iast: ātmānaṃ rathinaṃ viddhi śarīraṃ ratham eva tu
lines.deva: आत्मानं रथिनं विद्धि शरीरं रथमेव तु

lines.iast: buddhiṃ tu sārathiṃ viddhi manaḥ pragraham eva ca
lines.deva: बुद्धिं तु सारथिं विद्धि मनः प्रग्रहमेव च

padaccheda.iast: ātmānam rathinam viddhi śarīram ratham eva tu buddhim tu sārathim viddhi manaḥ pragraham eva ca
padaccheda.deva: आत्मानम् रथिनम् विद्धि शरीरम् रथम् एव तु बुद्धिम् तु सारथिम् विद्धि मनः प्रग्रहम् एव च

translations.text: “Know the self as the master of the chariot, and the body as the chariot. Know the intellect as the charioteer, and the mind as the reins.”

notes: Śaṅkara: the self meant here is the one bound to the cycle of birth and death, the ‘drinker’ of the first verse, who may travel either to liberation or onward in that cycle. The intellect is what determines; the mind is what forms intentions and doubts, and it holds the senses as reins hold horses.

sanskrit.iast:
indriyāṇi hayān āhur viṣayāṃsteṣu gocarān |
ātmendriyamanoyuktaṃ bhoktety āhur manīṣiṇaḥ || 4 ||

lines.iast: indriyāṇi hayān āhur viṣayāṃsteṣu gocarān
ātmendriyamanoyuktaṃ bhoktety āhur manīṣiṇaḥ

padaccheda.iast: indriyāṇi hayān āhuḥ viṣayān teṣu gocarān ātma-indriya-manaḥ-yuktam bhoktā iti āhuḥ manīṣiṇaḥ
padaccheda.deva: इन्द्रियाणि हयान् आहुः विषयान् तेषु गोचरान् आत्म-इन्द्रिय-मनः-युक्तम् भोक्ता इति आहुः मनीषिणः

words.meaning: joined with body, senses and mind

translations.text: “The senses, they say, are the horses, and the objects of the senses are the roads they travel. The self joined with body, senses and mind is what the wise call the enjoyer.”

notes: Śaṅkara: ātman in the compound means the body. The Self by itself is no enjoyer; it is an enjoyer only through the adjuncts of intellect and the rest. Only so can it be understood, further on, that the state of Viṣṇu is one's own Self.

sanskrit.deva:
यस्त्वविज्ञानवान्भवत्ययुक्तेन मनसा सदा ।
तस्येन्द्रियाण्यवश्यानि दुष्टाश्वा इव सारथेः ॥ ५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yas tv avijñānavān bhavaty ayuktena manasā sadā |
tasyendriyāṇy avaśyāni duṣṭāśvā iva sāratheḥ || 5 ||

lines.iast: yas tv avijñānavān bhavaty ayuktena manasā sadā
tasyendriyāṇy avaśyāni duṣṭāśvā iva sāratheḥ

padaccheda.iast: yaḥ tu a-vijñānavān bhavati ayuktena manasā sadā tasya indriyāṇi avaśyāni duṣṭa-aśvāḥ iva sāratheḥ
padaccheda.deva: यः तु अ-विज्ञानवान् भवति अयुक्तेन मनसा सदा तस्य इन्द्रियाणि अवश्यानि दुष्ट-अश्वाः इव सारथेः

translations.text: “But he who is without discernment, his mind always unrestrained: his senses are out of control, like the bad horses of a charioteer.”

notes: Śaṅkara: ‘without discernment’ is said of the charioteer, the intellect, when it is unskilled in what to pursue and what to avoid. The unrestrained mind is the reins not held.

sanskrit.deva:
यस्तु विज्ञानवान्भवति युक्तेन मनसा सदा ।
तस्येन्द्रियाणि वश्यानि सदश्वा इव सारथेः ॥ ६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yas tu vijñānavān bhavati yuktena manasā sadā |
tasyendriyāṇi vaśyāni sadaśvā iva sāratheḥ || 6 ||

lines.iast: yas tu vijñānavān bhavati yuktena manasā sadā
tasyendriyāṇi vaśyāni sadaśvā iva sāratheḥ

padaccheda.iast: yaḥ tu vijñānavān bhavati yuktena manasā sadā tasya indriyāṇi vaśyāni sat-aśvāḥ iva sāratheḥ
padaccheda.deva: यः तु विज्ञानवान् भवति युक्तेन मनसा सदा तस्य इन्द्रियाणि वश्यानि सत्-अश्वाः इव सारथेः

translations.text: “But he who has discernment, his mind always restrained: his senses are under control, like the good horses of a charioteer.”

notes: Śaṅkara: such senses can be set to work or drawn back at will, like well-trained horses.

sanskrit.deva:
यस्त्वविज्ञानवान्भवत्यमनस्कः सदाशुचिः ।
न स तत्पदमाप्नोति संसारं चाधिगच्छति ॥ ७ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yas tv avijñānavān bhavaty amanaskaḥ sadāśuciḥ |
na sa tat padam āpnoti saṃsāraṃ cādhigacchati || 7 ||

lines.iast: yas tv avijñānavān bhavaty amanaskaḥ sadāśuciḥ
na sa tat padam āpnoti saṃsāraṃ cādhigacchati

padaccheda.iast: yaḥ tu a-vijñānavān bhavati amanaskaḥ sadā aśuciḥ na saḥ tat padam āpnoti saṃsāram ca adhigacchati
padaccheda.deva: यः तु अ-विज्ञानवान् भवति अमनस्कः सदा अशुचिः न सः तत् पदम् आप्नोति संसारम् च अधिगच्छति

words.meaning: the cycle of birth and death

translations.text: “But he who is without discernment, his mind unrestrained and always impure, does not attain that goal; he goes on in the cycle of birth and death.”

notes: Śaṅkara: amanaska: one whose mind is not held in check, and who is for that reason always impure. ‘That goal’ is the imperishable supreme spoken of above.

sanskrit.deva:
यस्तु विज्ञानवान्भवति समनस्कः सदा शुचिः ।
स तु तत्पदमाप्नोति यस्माद्भूयो न जायते ॥ ८ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yas tu vijñānavān bhavati samanaskaḥ sadā śuciḥ |
sa tu tat padam āpnoti yasmād bhūyo na jāyate || 8 ||

lines.iast: yas tu vijñānavān bhavati samanaskaḥ sadā śuciḥ
sa tu tat padam āpnoti yasmād bhūyo na jāyate
lines.deva: स तु तत्पदमाप्नोति यस्माद्भूयो न जायते

padaccheda.iast: yaḥ tu vijñānavān bhavati samanaskaḥ sadā śuciḥ saḥ tu tat padam āpnoti yasmāt bhūyaḥ na jāyate
padaccheda.deva: यः तु विज्ञानवान् भवति समनस्कः सदा शुचिः सः तु तत् पदम् आप्नोति यस्मात् भूयः न जायते

translations.text: “But he who has discernment, his mind restrained and always pure, attains that goal from which he is not born again.”

notes: Śaṅkara: having reached that goal he does not fall from it, and so is not born again into the cycle of birth and death.

sanskrit.deva:
विज्ञानसारथिर्यस्तु मनःप्रग्रहवान्नरः ।
सोऽध्वनः पारमाप्नोति तद्विष्णोः परमं पदम् ॥ ९ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
vijñānasārathir yas tu manaḥpragrahavān naraḥ |
so 'dhvanaḥ pāram āpnoti tad viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam || 9 ||

lines.iast: vijñānasārathir yas tu manaḥpragrahavān naraḥ
so 'dhvanaḥ pāram āpnoti tad viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam

padaccheda.iast: vijñāna-sārathiḥ yaḥ tu manaḥ-pragrahavān naraḥ saḥ adhvanaḥ pāram āpnoti tat viṣṇoḥ paramam padam
padaccheda.deva: विज्ञान-सारथिः यः तु मनः-प्रग्रहवान् नरः सः अध्वनः पारम् आप्नोति तत् विष्णोः परमम् पदम्

words.meaning: who holds the reins of the mind

translations.text: “The man whose charioteer is discernment, and who holds the reins of the mind, reaches the end of the road: that highest state of Viṣṇu.”

notes: Śaṅkara: the road is the course of birth and death; reaching its end, he is freed from every bond. Viṣṇu is the all-pervading Brahman, the supreme Self, called Vāsudeva; his highest state is his true nature.

sanskrit.deva:
इन्द्रियेभ्यः परा ह्यर्था अर्थेभ्यश्च परं मनः ।
मनसस्तु परा बुद्धिर्बुद्धेरात्मा महान्परः ॥ १० ॥
sanskrit.iast:
indriyebhyaḥ parā hy arthā arthebhyaś ca paraṃ manaḥ |
manasas tu parā buddhir buddher ātmā mahān paraḥ || 10 ||

lines.iast: indriyebhyaḥ parā hy arthā arthebhyaś ca paraṃ manaḥ
lines.deva: इन्द्रियेभ्यः परा ह्यर्था अर्थेभ्यश्च परं मनः

lines.iast: manasas tu parā buddhir buddher ātmā mahān paraḥ

padaccheda.iast: indriyebhyaḥ parāḥ hi arthāḥ arthebhyaḥ ca param manaḥ manasaḥ tu parā buddhiḥ buddheḥ ātmā mahān paraḥ
padaccheda.deva: इन्द्रियेभ्यः पराः हि अर्थाः अर्थेभ्यः च परम् मनः मनसः तु परा बुद्धिः बुद्धेः आत्मा महान् परः

translations.text: “Higher than the senses are their objects, and higher than the objects is the mind. Higher than the mind is the intellect, and higher than the intellect is the great self.”

notes: Śaṅkara: ‘higher’ means subtler, greater and more inward. The objects are the subtle elements from which the senses are formed. Mind and intellect here stand for the subtle elements that give rise to them. The great self is the principle of Hiraṇyagarbha, the first-born of the unmanifest, the inner self of the intellects of all beings.

sanskrit.deva:
महतः परमव्यक्तमव्यक्तात्पुरुषः परः ।
पुरुषान्न परं किंचित्सा काष्ठा सा परा गतिः ॥ ११ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
mahataḥ param avyaktam avyaktāt puruṣaḥ paraḥ |
puruṣān na paraṃ kiṃcit sā kāṣṭhā sā parā gatiḥ || 11 ||

lines.iast: mahataḥ param avyaktam avyaktāt puruṣaḥ paraḥ
puruṣān na paraṃ kiṃcit sā kāṣṭhā sā parā gatiḥ
lines.deva: पुरुषान्न परं किंचित्सा काष्ठा सा परा गतिः

padaccheda.iast: mahataḥ param avyaktam avyaktāt puruṣaḥ paraḥ puruṣāt na param kiṃcit sā kāṣṭhā sā parā gatiḥ
padaccheda.deva: महतः परम् अव्यक्तम् अव्यक्तात् पुरुषः परः पुरुषात् न परम् किंचित् सा काष्ठा सा परा गतिः

translations.text: “Higher than the great is the unmanifest, and higher than the unmanifest is the Person. Higher than the Person there is nothing: that is the limit, that is the highest goal.”

notes: Śaṅkara: the unmanifest is the seed of the whole world, with name and form not yet unfolded, resting in the supreme Self as the power of a banyan tree rests in its seed. The Person is so called because he fills all (pūraṇāt). He is the limit at which subtlety, greatness and inwardness end, and the highest goal of all who travel in the cycle of birth and death.

sanskrit.deva:
एष सर्वेषु भूतेषु गूढोऽत्मा न प्रकाशते ।
दृश्यते त्वग्र्यया बुद्ध्या सूक्ष्मया सूक्ष्मदर्शिभिः ॥ १२ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
eṣa sarveṣu bhūteṣu gūḍho 'tmā na prakāśate |
dṛśyate tv agryayā buddhyā sūkṣmayā sūkṣmadarśibhiḥ || 12 ||

lines.iast: eṣa sarveṣu bhūteṣu gūḍho 'tmā na prakāśate
lines.deva: एष सर्वेषु भूतेषु गूढोऽत्मा न प्रकाशते

lines.iast: dṛśyate tv agryayā buddhyā sūkṣmayā sūkṣmadarśibhiḥ

padaccheda.iast: eṣaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu gūḍhaḥ ātmā na prakāśate dṛśyate tu agryayā buddhyā sūkṣmayā sūkṣma-darśibhiḥ
padaccheda.deva: एषः सर्वेषु भूतेषु गूढः आत्मा न प्रकाशते दृश्यते तु अग्र्यया बुद्ध्या सूक्ष्मया सूक्ष्म-दर्शिभिः

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. sg.

words.meaning: by those who see what is subtle

translations.text: “This Self, hidden in all beings, does not shine forth. But it is seen by those who see what is subtle, through a pointed and subtle intellect.”

notes: Śaṅkara: it is hidden in all beings, from Brahmā down to a tuft of grass, covered by ignorance and illusion in the form of seeing, hearing and other acts; so it does not show itself to anyone as the Self. Reaching it is called a ‘going’ only by a figure of speech: since it is the inmost Self of all, knowing it is the reaching. agryā: one-pointed, like the tip of a thing.

sanskrit.deva:
यच्छेद्वाङ्मनसी प्राज्ञस्तद्यच्छेज्ज्ञान आत्मनि ।
ज्ञानमात्मनि महति नियच्छेत्तद्यच्छेच्छान्त आत्मनि ॥ १३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yacched vāṅmanasī prājñas tad yacchej jñāna ātmani |
jñānam ātmani mahati niyacchet tad yacchecchānta ātmani || 13 ||

lines.iast: yacched vāṅmanasī prājñas tad yacchej jñāna ātmani
jñānam ātmani mahati niyacchet tad yacchecchānta ātmani

padaccheda.iast: yacchet vāk manasī prājñaḥ tat yacchet jñāne ātmani jñānam ātmani mahati niyacchet tat yacchet śānte ātmani
padaccheda.deva: यच्छेत् वाक् मनसी प्राज्ञः तत् यच्छेत् ज्ञाने आत्मनि ज्ञानम् आत्मनि महति नियच्छेत् तत् यच्छेत् शान्ते आत्मनि

translations.text: “The wise one should merge speech in the mind, and the mind in the knowing self, the intellect. He should merge the intellect in the great self, and that in the peaceful Self.”

notes: Śaṅkara: speech stands for all the senses. vāk is the accusative vācam with its ending dropped, and manasī is manasi with a Vedic long vowel. The ‘knowing self’ is the intellect, luminous by nature. The great self is the first-born. The peaceful Self is the principal Self, in which every distinction has ceased: changeless, inmost in all, witness of every thought.
The DCS takes vāṅmanasī as a compound, ‘speech and mind’; the analysis here follows Śaṅkara.

sanskrit.deva:
उत्तिष्ठत जाग्रत प्राप्य वरान्निबोधत ।
क्षुरस्य धारा निशिता दुरत्यया दुर्गं पथस्तत्कवयो वदन्ति ॥ १४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
uttiṣṭhata jāgrata prāpya varān nibodhata |
kṣurasya dhārā niśitā duratyayā durgaṃ pathas tat kavayo vadanti || 14 ||

lines.iast: uttiṣṭhata jāgrata prāpya varān nibodhata
kṣurasya dhārā niśitā duratyayā durgaṃ pathas tat kavayo vadanti
lines.deva: क्षुरस्य धारा निशिता दुरत्यया दुर्गं पथस्तत्कवयो वदन्ति

padaccheda.iast: uttiṣṭhata jāgrata prāpya varān nibodhata kṣurasya dhārā niśitā duratyayā durgam pathaḥ tat kavayaḥ vadanti
padaccheda.deva: उत्तिष्ठत जाग्रत प्राप्य वरान् निबोधत क्षुरस्य धारा निशिता दुरत्यया दुर्गम् पथः तत् कवयः वदन्ति

grammar.en: past passive participle f. nom. sg.

translations.text: “Arise! Awake! Approach the best of teachers and understand. Like the sharpened edge of a razor, hard to pass over: so hard to travel, the sages declare, is that path.”

notes: Śaṅkara: the Upaniṣad speaks out of compassion, like a mother: awake from the dreadful sleep of ignorance, the seed of every evil. ‘Understand’: know the inmost Self taught by them as ‘I am this’. pathaḥ is to be taken as panthānam, ‘the path’ of knowledge, which is hard to gain because what is to be known is so subtle.
The DCS reads varāt, an ablative; the text and Śaṅkara have varān, ‘the best’, which is followed here.

sanskrit.deva:
अशब्दमस्पर्शमरूपमव्ययं तथारसं नित्यमगन्धवच्च यत् ।
अनाद्यनन्तं महतः परं ध्रुवं निचाय्य तन्मृत्युमुखात्प्रमुच्यते ॥ १५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
aśabdam asparśam arūpam avyayaṃ tathārasaṃ nityam agandhavacca yat |
anādy anantaṃ mahataḥ paraṃ dhruvaṃ nicāyya tan mṛtyumukhāt pramucyate || 15 ||

lines.iast: aśabdam asparśam arūpam avyayaṃ tathārasaṃ nityam agandhavacca yat
anādy anantaṃ mahataḥ paraṃ dhruvaṃ nicāyya tan mṛtyumukhāt pramucyate
lines.deva: अनाद्यनन्तं महतः परं ध्रुवं निचाय्य तन्मृत्युमुखात्प्रमुच्यते

padaccheda.iast: aśabdam asparśam arūpam avyayam tathā arasam nityam a-gandhavat ca yat anādi anantam mahataḥ param dhruvam nicāyya tat mṛtyu-mukhāt pramucyate
padaccheda.deva: अशब्दम् अस्पर्शम् अरूपम् अव्ययम् तथा अरसम् नित्यम् अ-गन्धवत् च यत् अनादि अनन्तम् महतः परम् ध्रुवम् निचाय्य तत् मृत्यु-मुखात् प्रमुच्यते

translations.text: “That which is without sound, touch, form, taste or smell, undecaying and eternal, without beginning or end, higher than the great, and unchanging: realising that, one is released from the jaws of death.”

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: how is what is to be known so subtle? The earth is gross, having sound, touch, form, taste and smell, an object of all the senses; so is the body. As these qualities drop away one by one, from water up to space, greater subtlety, extent, purity and permanence are seen. What need to say that subtlety is unsurpassed in that in which none of them, from smell to sound, is found?

Śaṅkara: whatever has sound and the other qualities decays; Brahman, having none, does not. Without beginning: it has no cause into which it could dissolve; without end: it has no effect by producing which it would perish. ‘The great’ here is the principle called intellect. The jaws of death are ignorance, desire and action.

sanskrit.deva:
नाचिकेतमुपाख्यानं मृत्युप्रोक्तं सनातनम् ।
उक्त्वा श्रुत्वा च मेधावी ब्रह्मलोके महीयते ॥ १६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
nāciketam upākhyānaṃ mṛtyuproktaṃ sanātanam |
uktvā śrutvā ca medhāvī brahmaloke mahīyate || 16 ||

lines.iast: nāciketam upākhyānaṃ mṛtyuproktaṃ sanātanam
uktvā śrutvā ca medhāvī brahmaloke mahīyate
lines.deva: उक्त्वा श्रुत्वा च मेधावी ब्रह्मलोके महीयते

padaccheda.iast: nāciketam upākhyānam mṛtyu-proktam sanātanam uktvā śrutvā ca medhāvī brahma-loke mahīyate
padaccheda.deva: नाचिकेतम् उपाख्यानम् मृत्यु-प्रोक्तम् सनातनम् उक्त्वा श्रुत्वा च मेधावी ब्रह्म-लोके महीयते

words.meaning: in the world that is Brahman

translations.text: A wise person who tells, and who hears, this ancient story of Naciketas, told by Death, is honoured in the world that is Brahman.

notes: Śaṅkara: the Upaniṣad says this in praise of the teaching. The story is the three vallīs; it is ‘ancient’ because it is Vedic. It is told to brahmins and heard from teachers. brahmaloka: the world which is Brahman itself.

sanskrit.deva:
य इमं परमं गुह्यं श्रावयेद्ब्रह्मसंसदि ।
प्रयतः श्राद्धकाले वा तदानन्त्याय कल्पते ।
तदानन्त्याय कल्पत इति ॥ १७ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
ya imaṃ paramaṃ guhyaṃ śrāvayed brahmasaṃsadi |
prayataḥ śrāddhakāle vā tad ānantyāya kalpate |
tad ānantyāya kalpata iti || 17 ||

lines.iast: ya imaṃ paramaṃ guhyaṃ śrāvayed brahmasaṃsadi
prayataḥ śrāddhakāle vā tad ānantyāya kalpate
tad ānantyāya kalpata iti

padaccheda.iast: yaḥ imam paramam guhyam śrāvayet brahma-saṃsadi prayataḥ śrāddha-kāle vā tat ānantyāya kalpate tat ānantyāya kalpate iti
padaccheda.deva: यः इमम् परमम् गुह्यम् श्रावयेत् ब्रह्म-संसदि प्रयतः श्राद्ध-काले वा तत् आनन्त्याय कल्पते तत् आनन्त्याय कल्पते इति

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. sg.

words.meaning: at the time of the rite for the ancestors

translations.text: Whoever, having purified himself, recites this supreme secret in an assembly of brahmins, or at the time of the rite for the ancestors: that leads to an endless reward, that leads to an endless reward.

notes: Śaṅkara: recited both in its words and in its meaning. The repetition marks the end of the adhyāya.
